2014 - the year that was

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A review of the events that changed the world in the last year

Summary:
A review of major world events that made history in 2014, and a brief analysis do how they changed the world and shaped people's attitudes. Events will include politics and elections, disasters and accidents, business and the economy, law and crime, armed conflicts, arts and culture, science and technology, sport and a mention of the famous people who died this year.

Further information:
There will be a mix of international and local events depending on which were more influential and memorable in the minds of South Africans, and a brief analysis from a news editor, political analyst, technological and others Xperia as to why and how these events were game-changers.
A combination of news footage and existing Carte Blanche footage will be used. There may be previous Carte Blanche stories that covered world events and those stories that were highlights of the year. The review would include stories like the Public Protectors report on Nkandla, the Oscar Pistorius trial, the SA General elections and the birth of the EFF, the disappearance of flight MH370, the FIFA World Cup in Brazil, the conflict in Gaza, the downing of flight MH17 in Ukraine, the emergence of ISIS and Jihad John, the collapse of TB Joshua's SCOAN building, the outbreak of Ebola in West Africa, the landin of Philae on comet 76P, the killing of Senzo Meyiwa, the death of Robin Williams and JoanRivers, etc

News footage

Mr. Toby Shapshak

Johannesburg

News footage of world events

Press Release:


Newsmakers 2014
“Have you heard the one about Radovan Krejcir? He has a higher fatality rate than Ebola in the US” – Nick Rabinowitz. South African comedians give Carte Blanche a witty take on the news and events of 2014.


Script:


2014 – THE YEAR IN REVIEW

Amanda: Well, Eskom darkness, Ebola plague, I mean every sign is there that this is the end of the world, 2014. What can we expect? Ebolus eventualis had to come.

Nik: I appreciate it when they put a gate on the end of a scandal. You know Nkandlagate: this one you must look a: Oilgate, Travelgate, Oscardoor.

E-tolls montage

Joey: So the thing about e-tolls is that it’s nice decorations on the highway now, especially on the N1 and the R24, it’s nice – the blue lights.

David: About a million people marched against e-tolls – that first big march that Zwelinzima Vavi organized - and about 900 000 of those people don’t even have cars.

Nik: COSATU of course had that go-slow, that was fantastic. Remember that? Was it the M1? They had the go-slow, and then a coup0le of weeks later Zwelinzima Vavi had a - cos the go-slow was on the M1, but he had a quickie on his desk. Which I thought should have been a go-slow, but it wasn’t. And she was like in-tray, out-tray, in-tray, out-tray, and after that NUMSA wanted to pull out, which is what Vavi should have done. And then Irvin Jim was like no we’re pulling out, NUMSA’s pulling out. And then Vavi was like no, stay, please stay. And then Irvin was like no, Zweli. No means no.

Amanda: Yes but e-tolls. Do you remember the word, or are you too young? Tol, are you a tol, are you a tollie, are you a gomtollie? I mean tol means rubbish. Why will you give your money to the gom tollies? Here’s my money tol. The only tol who made money this year was Radovan Krejicir.

Radovan Krejicir montage

Nik: Radovan Krejicir they call him the one-man crime wave. How many people connected to him – was it a dozen – died in the last couple of years? Basically he’s got a higher fatality rate than Ebola in the US.

Amanda: How many mamparas in the prison at the same time? I mean they can close down Waterkloof Country Club. Close it down. There is Oscar mampara with Krejicir mampara with those two Waterkloof mampara.

Nik: They’re in the same wing of the Schabir Shaik Memorial Ward of the Pretoria Prison.

Oscar Trial montage:

Nik: There are 2 murders that you don’t commit, ok. The one is you don’t kill a White woman or a Black rhino. Those are the ones you don’t do.

Amanda I mean the drama that he put on! You know he had no training. In the past we had OJ Simpson – what a performance he gave in the court, big performance, but he had practiced. He had Naked Gun. Naked Gun was a runaway hit. Without any practice Oscar took the show.

Nik: I was very anxious Milady. It was dark outside, it was dark inside, I thought there was a darkie in the bathroom.

Amanda: I mean better than Robert de Niro that performance, we have to say.

Nik: Now he’s joined the 28’s, apparently he’s joined the 28’s gang in prison. They’re walking around going “Oscar! Aweh silver bene!“

Nkandla montage

Joey: How can you not know people is building in your house? I can’t understand that. How can I not know that you people are interviewing me? There’s a light here. You put up this light.

Amanda: We should start the Virgin Active there in Nkandla. Everybody could use that fire pool beautifully. Come out slim, svelte.

Nik: Or I think a better idea, is to turn Nkandla into B&B, and basically to offer every South African 2 days of timeshare a year, and that way we pay back. I don’t want to go in summer. And I want a window- facing the fire pool - unless Khulabusi is there. Then I don’t want any windows. I must be in the basement- with Ma Khumalo- and then we’re going to chat and watch the Generations omnibus with choccies and gossip about other wives and their stupid hair. We’re going to be like “Ja, you must tell wives 3 and 4 they must take their weave and leave.”


General Election montage

David: The kiss- I think actually made it ridiculous. Otherwise it would have just stayed as another failed attempt at two parties partnering. But I think the kiss between those two old ladies…

Amanda: That kiss – I think it outdid who was the famous kiss? Britney and Madonna. It was honestly in a league of hilarity like none other. MTV has never come close to anything as ridiculous and controversial.

Nik: Do you remember Mamphele Ramphele? “I’m sorry that you weren’t smart enough to know I was the one to lead the country. And I will always cherish the successes and failures - not so much failures. But we should think of them as shared failures. Some of them were mine but others were also your fault. And now I must go and spend time with family, reconnecting with old friends . Helen still doesn’t answer my calls. “Helzi, it’s me!”

EFF in parliament montage

Joey: If you look at Cope, shame. Then Agang, I don’t know. Then we have the EFF.

Nik: They of course got 6 percent of vote and 100 percent overalls, which is a wonderful achievement. They’ve done a lot to promote the parliamentary channel, the ratings never been this good. And then they heckled the speaker out. She was like “I don’t recognize you, I don’t’ recognize you, I can’t even recognize you” - cos she had dementia. By the end of the day they’d had 4 speakers, right. If they could have just added another speaker and a subwoofer, that would’ve been the biggest house party of 2014.

Spy Tapes montage:

David: NPA came and said “Oh, we found tapes. We found tapes. We’re dropping the charges.”
What tapes? Can we hear the tapes?
“You can’t hear the tapes, we are rewinding the tapes.”
This is how Black people rewind tapes by the way.

Russian nuclear deal montage:

Nik: The Russians are going to come and install – I think it’s eight nuclear power reactors. I think we’ve got to find out which province it’s not going to be in so we can move there. Make it Limpopo please - I don’t know, I’m just saying. And it was signed by Tina Jouma-se-Pietersen.

And we’ve actually got a new Xhosa dictionary as well where the word “nuclear”, the Xhosa version is in there. Did you see that? “iNuclear”.

Dewani montage:

Amanda: For me Dewani could take over in the next role from Meryl Streep as The Devil Wears Prada.

Nik: His username on Gaydar, or the other one, can’t remember, is Asian Sub. Which in my day used to be the 12th man for India.

Dalai Lama montage

Nik: You know who I felt for was Clayson Monyela. You know when you have to deliver that same speech that you did 2 years ago, and it was uncomfortable the first time, and now you must come back, and you you’ve got to again ap0ologise? It wasn’t even your decision, but you have to be like …”Our official p0osition vis-à-vis the the, the visa, blah, blah, blah, based on what we’ve said in the past, blah, blah, blah, whereby what we are going to say in the future relates to what we are currently saying in the the, the, the, the, the, the present.”

The Arch we know was very upset, again I think he had a press conference didn’t he? : “We are just, we are really very disappointed in our government. You know it just harks back to the age, to the apartheid. What, what, what, what, what, what are we doing? It’s just outrageous.”

David: I know that where there’s comedy there’s hope.

End of Year montage
